To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

consumers’ preferences for tangerines, satsumas, or clementines were related to internal quality of the fruit, and that consumers’ preferences could be predicted based on internal quality and other consumer characteristics.

1) tangerines were the most preferred, followed by satsumas and clementines; 2) consumers preferred mandarin types that are high in soluble solids and low in acidity; 3) mandarin type preference is not influenced by demographic characteristics; 4) mandarin type preferences are influenced by the purchase frequency of mandarins; 5) the probability of preferring tangerines was 2.5 times higher than the probability of preferring clementines; and
consumers’ preferences for mandarin varieties are influenced by internal quality, demographic, and purchase factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for predicting consumer preference of fresh mandarin oranges based on internal quality analysis and consumer sensory evaluation.
the development of a consumer-based quality index for mandarins and with the use of the index in a model to predict mandarin preferences.
consumer preferences for mandarins and how these preferences relate to the internal quality of mandarins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
consumers preferred tangerines and satsumas over clementines, and that consumers with a preference for tangerines or clementines had different demographic profiles.
the satsumas are preferred over the tangerines by 1.6 to 1, and the clementines are preferred by 0.6 to 0.7 to 1 over the tangerine and satsuma.

the tangerine is preferred by the majority of the consumers, followed by satsuma and clementine, and that there is a strong relationship between the Brix-to-acids ratio of the fruit and the consumers’ preference for that fruit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
consumers prefer the tangerine and satsuma varieties, and that the Brix-to-acit ratio can be used as a quality indicator for satsuma mandarins.
consumers are willing to pay a premium for mandarins with a high Brix-to-acit ratio, and that the premium is higher for satsumas and clementines than for tangerines.
consumer preferences for the three mandarins are related to internal quality, which is related to the Brix-to-acidity ratios, and that the Brix-to- acidity ratios are related to harvest standards.
The main takeaway from our work is that
consumer preferences are driven more by internal quality than by external appearance, and that the internal quality of mandarins is affected by the time of year of harvest.
the consumer preferences for mandarins can be predicted by internal quality analysis of the fruit.
consumers are not always able to identify the type of mandarin they prefer.
